# Psalm 64 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. A-psalm of-David.

**2** Hear my-voice, O-God, in-my-complaint; from-the-dread of-the-enemy preserve my-life.

**3** Hide-me from-the-counsel of-evildoers, from-the-tumult of-workers of-iniquity,

**4** who-sharpen their-tongue like-a-sword, [who] aim their-arrow — a-bitter word —

**5** to-shoot in-hiding at-the-blameless. Suddenly they-shoot-him and-do-not fear.

**6** They-strengthen for-themselves an-evil purpose; they-talk of-hiding snares; they-say, 'Who sees-them?'

**7** They-search-out injustices: 'We-have-completed a-searched-out search!' And-the-inward-part of-a-man and-the-heart [is] deep.

**8** But-God shoots-them [with] an-arrow; suddenly their-wounds [come].

**9** And-they-cause-him-to-stumble — upon-them their-tongue; all who-see-them flee.

**10** And-all men fear and-declare the-work of-God, and-His-deed they-understand.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **64:8**: Poetic justice: they aimed arrows (v.4); God shoots arrows at them (v.8). The weapon returns on the attacker.

— EMET
